questions.q: What message did Isaiah receive from Yahweh?
questions.a: He received a message about Babylon.

questions.q: What should be lifted up on the bare hill?
questions.a: A banner should be lifted up to signal an army to attack Babylon.

questions.q: What has Yahweh called his warriors to do?
questions.a: He has called them to attack the Babylonians because he is angry with them.

questions.q: What sound comes from the mountains?
questions.a: The sound of a huge army, because Yahweh is gathering soldiers from many kingdoms for battle.

questions.q: From where does Yahweh’s army come?
questions.a: They come from distant lands, from the farthest places under the sky.

questions.q: What will Yahweh’s weapons do?
questions.a: They will destroy the whole land of Babylonia.

questions.q: What should the people do because the day of Yahweh is near?
questions.a: They should wail, because Yahweh, the Almighty God, will destroy them.

questions.q: What will happen to the Babylonians when the land is destroyed?
questions.a: They will lose their courage and become weak with fear. They will feel much anguish and move around in pain like a woman giving birth. They will look at each other in shock, their faces red with shame.

questions.q: What else will happen during the day of Yahweh?
questions.a: The land will be made desolate and the sinners will be destroyed from it. The stars, constellations, sun and moon will not give their light; they will be darkened.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to the wicked and the proud?
questions.a: He will punish the world for its evil, punish wicked people for their sins, and humble the proud and arrogant.

questions.q: Will there be many men left?
questions.a: No, Yahweh will make people rarer than fine gold, harder to find than the gold of Ophir.

questions.q: What will happen to the heavens and the earth?
questions.a: They will tremble and shake because of Yahweh’s anger.

questions.q: What will the foreigners in Babylon do?
questions.a: They will flee back to their own homeland and people, like a hunted gazelle or a flock of sheep with no shepherd.

questions.q: What will happen to anyone who is found or caught?
questions.a: They will be killed by the sword.

questions.q: What will happen to the houses in Babylon?
questions.a: They will be plundered of their valuable possessions.

questions.q: Who is Yahweh going to stir up to attack the Babylonians?
questions.a: Yahweh is going to stir up the Medes to attack the Babylonians.

questions.q: Who will the Medes’ bows kill?
questions.a: They will kill the young men, and the Medes will not spare children or babies.

questions.q: What will happen to Babylon?
questions.a: God will destroy Babylon completely, just as he destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, and no one will ever live there again.

questions.q: What will lie in Babylon?
questions.a: Wild animals of the desert will lie there.

questions.q: When will these things happen to Babylon?
questions.a: These things will happen soon; Babylon’s days will not be delayed.

commentary.text: The armies of God's wrath. (Is. 13:1-5) The conquest of Babylon. (Is. 13:6-18) Its final desolation. (Is. 13:19-22)

Is. 13:1-5 The threatenings of God's word press heavily upon the wicked, and are a sore burden, too heavy for them to bear. The persons brought together to lay Babylon waste, are called God's sanctified or appointed ones; designed for this service, and made able to do it. They are called God's mighty ones, because they had their might from God, and were now to use it for him. They come from afar. God can make those a scourge and ruin to his enemies, who are farthest off, and therefore least dreaded.

Is. 13:6-18 We have here the terrible desolation of Babylon by the Medes and Persians. Those who in the day of their peace were proud, and haughty, and terrible, are quite dispirited when trouble comes. Their faces shall be scorched with the flame. All comfort and hope shall fail. The stars of heaven shall not give their light, the sun shall be darkened. Such expressions are often employed by the prophets, to describe the convulsions of governments. God will visit them for their iniquity, particularly the sin of pride, which brings men low. There shall be a general scene of horror. Those who join themselves to Babylon, must expect to share her plagues, Rev. 18:4. All that men have, they would give for their lives, but no man's riches shall be the ransom of his life. Pause here and wonder that men should be thus cruel and inhuman, and see how corrupt the nature of man is become. And that little infants thus suffer, which shows that there is an original guilt, by which life is forfeited as soon as it is begun. The day of the Lord will, indeed, be terrible with wrath and fierce anger, far beyond all here stated. Nor will there be any place for the sinner to flee to, or attempt an escape. But few act as though they believed these things.

Is. 13:19-22 Babylon was a noble city; yet it should be wholly destroyed. None shall dwell there. It shall be a haunt for wild beasts. All this is fulfilled. The fate of this proud city is a proof of the truth of the Bible, and an emblem of the approaching ruin of the New Testament Babylon; a warning to sinners to flee from the wrath to come, and it encourages believers to expect victory over every enemy of their souls, and of the church of God. The whole world changes and is liable to decay. Wherefore let us give diligence to obtain a kingdom which cannot be moved; and in this hope let us hold fast that grace whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear.
